candidates.name: OpportunityInsights/EconomicTracker
candidates.what_it_holds: The official 'Track the Recovery' repo (Chetty/Friedman/Hendren/Stepner/team, Harvard/Opportunity Insights). data/ folder has committed CSVs at National/State/County/City x Daily/Monthly granularity for Affinity Solutions credit/debit card spending ('Affinity - National - Daily.csv', 'Affinity - State - Daily.csv', 'Affinity - County - Daily.csv', 'Affinity - City - Daily.csv', plus Monthly variants, and 'Affinity Income Shares' / 'Affinity Industry Composition' breakout files by income quartile and industry, back to Jan 2020 with a 2019 pre-period baseline index). Repo also bundles other Track-the-Recovery series (Womply small-business revenue/open, Burning Glass job postings, Zillow rent) in the same data/ tree per its data dictionary, 1,892+ commits, actively updated. Docs include a Data Dictionary (md + PDF), Data Documentation (source/processing notes), and a Data Revisions log (evidence of point-in-time-ish revision tracking, worth checking for vintage use). Data is a public good; must credit provider + cite the paper (https://opportunityinsights.org / tracktherecovery.org), no resale/redistribution to third parties as raw data.
candidates.why_useful: Directly targets gap #6 (public consumer-spend panels, explicitly named in the gap list). Daily/county-level card spend by industry (leisure & hospitality / entertainment / accommodation likely broken out via the industry-composition files) is a US consumer-strength nowcast input finer-grained than BEA PCE travel or FRED CPI, and could proxy discretionary/travel spend swings ahead of ABNB's North America nights print. The Data Revisions log is worth checking against rule #2 (point-in-time) before use.
candidates.time_coverage: Jan 2020 - present (daily), with a Jan 2019-Feb 2020 baseline period; updated on an ongoing cadence (1,892+ commits)
candidates.size_hint: Multiple CSVs per geography x frequency combination; county-daily file alone likely hundreds of thousands of rows
candidates.license: Custom 'public good' terms: free to use with attribution to data provider(s) + citation of the OI paper; no resale or third-party redistribution of raw underlying data
candidates.last_activity: Actively maintained (commit count in the thousands; exact latest date not confirmed via fetch)

candidates.name: dbnomics/rdbnomics
candidates.what_it_holds: R client (also has Python/other-language siblings) for the DBnomics API (api.db.nomics.world), which aggregates time series from ~90+ national and international statistical providers (Eurostat, IMF, World Bank, ECB, and many national statistical offices/central banks) into one queryable API via rdb(), rdb_datasets(), rdb_providers(). On CRAN and GitHub, 36 stars, 104 commits, mirrored from git.nomics.world. Does not itself contain UK ONS / Banco de Portugal / Norges Bank card-spending series as committed files, but DBnomics as a platform is a single point to check whether those agencies' series (including any card/payment statistics they publish) are mirrored and pullable programmatically.
candidates.why_useful: A one-API acquisition method to probe for point-in-time-style pulls of European national-statistics series (potential CHAPS/SIBS/Norges Bank-adjacent series if those agencies publish to DBnomics), relevant to gaps #4 and #6; needs a follow-up check of rdb_providers() output to confirm ONS/BdP/Norges Bank coverage before relying on it.
candidates.geography: Global (provider list includes many European national statistical offices/central banks per DBnomics' own description)
candidates.size_hint: N/A - API client, not a static dataset
candidates.license: Not confirmed on the fetched page (CRAN package; DBnomics platform itself is open data / AGPL-family per its own site, not independently verified here)
candidates.last_activity: Active CRAN package; exact last-commit date not shown on fetched page

candidates.name: ooi-darren/project-007-global-consumer-spending
candidates.what_it_holds: MIT-licensed, 10-commit repo with a 182-country annual consumer-spending panel (data/processed/master_consumer_spending.csv), 2013-2023, built from World Bank household consumption expenditure/GDP/population/urbanisation/internet-penetration data, World Bank Worldwide Governance Indicators, and OECD 12-category (COICOP) household spending shares for 36 countries (category_spending_shares_oecd.csv), plus a latest_year_snapshot.csv and a UN M49 region-mapping file. No isolated travel/tourism/accommodation spend category confirmed; annual frequency only.
candidates.why_useful: Marginal: annual, country-level, non-point-in-time macro consumption data that mostly duplicates World Bank/OECD/Eurostat series the team likely already has cheaper access to (and does not isolate travel spend); the COICOP category-share file for 36 countries could be a minor cross-check for discretionary-spend share trends by country, but nothing here is finer-grained or more current than existing holdings.
candidates.size_hint: Small (~182 rows x few dozen columns for the main panel; ~36 rows for category shares)
candidates.last_activity: 10 commits total; recent given repo is a 2026-era portfolio project, exact date not confirmed
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: Overlaps with existing Eurostat/BEA PCE/OECD consumer-confidence holdings; adds little

candidates.name: api-evangelist/txn
candidates.what_it_holds: A documentation/profile repo (part of Kin Lane's 'API Evangelist' API-directory project) describing TXN Solutions Inc., a San Francisco fintech that captures consumer transactions directly from credit/debit cards for spending analytics and competitive intelligence. Contains no data files itself, only a write-up/profile pointing at TXN's commercial product (https://txnsolutions.com or similar, not independently verified).
candidates.why_useful: Not itself a data source - flags a commercial (licensed, likely paid) card-transaction data vendor that could be worth a human licensing conversation, but nothing free or open is in the repo.
candidates.time_coverage: Unknown - vendor product, not a static dataset
candidates.license: Unknown / commercial vendor, repo itself likely CC/MIT for the write-up only

notes: This run hit hard tooling limits: the shared WebSearch budget for the session was already exhausted (200/200) before any of my queries ran, so I could not do the standard site:github.com / 'dataset csv' keyword sweep at all. github.com/search (the built-in GitHub search UI, fetched via WebFetch rather than the disallowed `gh search`) returned HTTP 429 Too Many Requests (Retry-After 3600) on every attempt, likely from other scouts hammering the same endpoint concurrently. Bing and DuckDuckGo via WebFetch were also unproductive: Bing's fetched page returned unrelated cached content (travel ads, German Wikipedia) rather than live results, and DuckDuckGo's HTML endpoint served a bot-check CAPTCHA. As a result this scout relied on direct WebFetch of known/likely repo and org URLs from training knowledge rather than search-driven discovery, which is far narrower than the intended method. Confirmed dead ends: github.com/bankofengland has just a profile-config repo, no CHAPS/payments data; github.com/BBVA's visible repos are all engineering tooling (Kapow, apicheck, mercury-*), nothing consumer-spend related visible in the first page; github.com/Norges-Bank is behind an SSO wall and unreachable via WebFetch; opentable/state-of-industry-data does not exist at that path and OpenTable's visible GitHub repos are all backend/infra tooling, not the public 'State of the Industry' dining data (which OpenTable publishes as a web page/PDF, not a GitHub-committed dataset, as far as I could verify). I found nothing at all for ONS card spending / Faster Indicators, Banco de Portugal SIBS, or CaixaBank Research as GitHub repos - could not confirm they exist OR confirm they don't, given the search-tool outage. RECOMMENDATION for a follow-up scout with working search: re-run this theme once WebSearch quota resets or `gh search` capacity frees up; specifically chase (a) 'ONS' + 'faster indicators' + 'experimental statistics' + github, (b) 'SIBS Analytics' or 'Banco de Portugal' + 'estatisticas' + github, (c) 'Norges Bank' + 'betalingsstatistikk' (Norwegian for payment statistics) + github, (d) BIS CPMI Red Book statistics (covers card payment volumes for Portugal/Norway/Spain/UK in one place) for a github mirror or API client, (e) rdb_providers() output from the dbnomics client to see if any of ONS/BdP/Norges Bank series are actually mirrored there before treating rdbnomics as more than a maybe.
